[1] Thresh is a skill matchup, a fun skill matchup. The way we look at this matchup is: if you ult while he has lantern up, he wins. If he lanterns before you, then you win. It's a patience game.
[1] Obviously, you don't want to get hooked. He doesn't want to get Q'd. Basically, none of those things should ever happen cuz you kind of just face each other.
[1] So, it just comes down to who uses their W or Q first. Whoever uses it first will lose.
[2] He is not so strong in lane but he will outroam you so try to get an advantage on botlane when he is missing and punish him for leaving his poor adc alone against Thresh
[2] If he lands the stun on both you and your ADC, say goodbye to your HP. That being said Bard is very squishy and if you land the hook you can kill him 9 times out of 10.
[2] Remember to position yourself away from other entities that will get you stunned while trying to land a hook.
[2] Post 6, make sure that you and your ADC avoid his ultimate as you will be one of the only sources for them to recover with your dark passage.
[2] Bard is relatively squishy, landing a hook on him will/should force his sums and win the trade massively. Avoid being close to minions, ally champions or walls to avoid stunned.
[2] Out of lane you can save allies from his ULT with lanturn.
[2] Look for hooks on him since he is a very squishy champion, but if you miss then play more passive. Try to follow his roams and signal mia when he is not in lane.
[2] More often than not, Bard will also roam and leave his ADC vulnerable earlier than most supports.
[3] Because BARD is not a tank and doesn't have that much durability. If caught with a threat hook, bard will not be able to use the E skill to escape from the situation.

[3] If thresh hooks your ally, you have a lot of options to work with. Usually though, he's looking to make a pick, so don't hesitate to ult him or an enemy. You also generally want to wait if lantern is out before using your ult.
[3] Hook champions :( play safe and punish important cds
